analysis.title: Marketcolour + HF Performance / Flows / Kering / Safran / Elux / Volvo / Sika / Signify
key_insights: US equities closed sharply lower on 10/22 with focus on rates and oil: SPX -121bps to 7663, NDX -290bps to 28958 (lower on 9 of 12 sessions), DJIA +2bps to 52867, VIX +13.7% to 18.49. The 10Y UST fell 15bps to 4.95%, the largest move of the year, and oil returned to ytd highs.

Sector moves in the US were wide: Staples -331bps, Tech -329bps, Comm svs -142bps, Utilities +207bps. In Europe, Defensives (GSXEDEFS) rose 1.8% on Pharma (+2.5%) and Staples (+2.0%) earnings beats, and Bond Proxies (GSXEBOND) rose 1.3%.

The SOX has underperformed the S&P 500 by 13% over the last 9 sessions since Mon 10/12, the biggest 9-day underperformance stretch in 20+ years. The SOX is testing its 200-dma for the first time since June 2025.

Dispersion was extreme: 155 S&P names had moves of 2.0 sigma or more, the highest since the May 2025 US-China tariff truce, while 335 S&P names finished higher on the day. GS describes this as one of the widest gaps between S&P breadth and index performance going back to the 1990s.

The AI basket (GSTMTAIP) is down 23% from its June highs, a similar drawdown to the one seen before the July bounce. High Beta Momentum (GSPRHIMO) has erased all its ytd gains (it was +70% in June), driven by the AI-correlated long leg. SPX ex-AI (SPXXAI) has outperformed the S&P by 6% MTD.

GS saw no sign of offense being played around the AI theme on its flow pad on 10/22. Last week's rotational flows out of AI into defensives were largely absent, despite gains in Consumer, Utilities and parts of Financials.

GS PB data: Fundamental L/S down 1.1% (-1.7sd), Systematics down 1.2% (-3.2sd), Multi-Strats down 1.4% (-2.5sd). This was the first time since Covid that all three strategies fell more than 1% on the same day.
The GS HF Positioning Pair (GSTHVIPP) fell about 4.2%, its worst move since 2011, and is down 10.4% MTD.
Kering Q3 2026: Gucci retail was -9% on constant FX, a miss. GS cut its target price 8% and stays Neutral.

Safran Q3 first take: revenues in line with consensus. Propulsion and Interiors were 1% light and Equipment & Defence 3% ahead. Spares and Services growth slowed to +17% and +19%, and guidance is unchanged at mid-twenties growth for both. GS indicates the stock -2% after GE fell 3.5% despite raising guidance.

Electrolux Q3: like-for-like growth +3.5%, North America +2.4% vs consensus -2.1%. Adjusted EBIT was a 5% beat on smaller N Am losses and LatAm ahead of expectations. Guidance on price/cost moderated to neutral from positive.

Volvo Q3: profit in line on strong CE and Penta, while Trucks missed by 6% on softer revenue and slightly weaker margins. The FX tailwind was 970 vs GSe 350, with a small net tariff benefit of +0.2bn. Orders were in line with consensus but 12% below GS estimates. 2027 market guidance is Europe flattish and N Am up about 13%, more bullish on N Am than expected.

Sika Q3: organic growth +4.6%, a slowdown from +6% in Q2 but ahead of consensus +4%. FY26 guidance reiterated. Gross margin was flat y/y and stronger than expected despite oil-based input costs. EMEA grew +6%.
Signify: messy Q3 print distorted by tariff refunds, underlying business still seeing estimate downgrades. The stock trades near lows, and GS sees no fundamental reason for a bounce (indication -2%).

Momentum has broken below support and retested its September lows. Unconstrained Momentum (GSPRHIMO) is in its worst drawdown since the GFC apart from Covid. The Prime Book is reducing Momentum exposure and increasing Profitability exposure.
